competing_hypotheses.hypothesis: Some or all of the Bitquery collector-directed dust payments are included in t54's x402 merchant transaction counts.
support: Three exact destination addresses overlap between the t54 merchant directory and Bitquery collector addresses.
disconfirming_or_missing: No raw SourceTag 804681468 and transaction-hash join; same destination can receive both tagged x402 and unrelated payments.

competing_hypotheses.hypothesis: The addresses are valid x402 merchant destinations, but the Bitquery dust transactions are unrelated inbound transfers and are not x402 facilitator events.
support: XRPL Payment destinations can receive transactions outside the x402 facilitator; the source-tag join is absent.
disconfirming_or_missing: The public directory and Bitquery use the same exact addresses, so transaction-level separation is still required.

competing_hypotheses.hypothesis: Address-level transaction counts overstate actual merchant/customer activity because unrelated transfers, dust and automated calls can share merchant destinations.
support: Bitquery reports 99.6% of RLUSD payments in its window going to three collector addresses; t54 directory ranks merchant addresses by transaction count.
disconfirming_or_missing: A complete t54 raw-event export and independent validated-ledger classification are unavailable.

competing_hypotheses.hypothesis: The high transaction count reflects genuine low-ticket API/machine payments but remains economically small at aggregate scale.
support: t54 dashboard reports $48,848 over 14,850,938 all-time settlements; the calculated average is approximately $0.00329 per reported event.
disconfirming_or_missing: The dashboard's value/count definitions, event deduplication and source-tag completeness are not independently reconciled.

prediction_policy.reason: Transaction count, merchant count, live-service count and gross stablecoin transfer value are not substitutes for net external settlement value or XRP inventory demand.
required_features: unique paying accounts and unique merchant accounts
delivered value by asset and issuer
median and distribution of ticket size
issuer mint/burn and cross-chain bridge adjustments
XRP bridge-route share and net inventory change
point-in-time ledger index and source snapshot hash
